name: Bangolan

tone_statements.citation: Njeck, Mathaus Mbah. 2004. Bangolan Orthography Statement. Yaoundé: NACALCO.
tone_statements.quote: We have identified six surface tones in Bangolan: three level tones, high [á], mid [ā] and low [à]; and three contour tones, rising [ǎ], high-falling [â], and low-falling [ȁ]. ... As of this point in time, we have discovered numerous minimal tone pairs for words that contrast high tone, rising tone and high-falling tone with each other or with either of the two low tones. ... Tone also plays an important role in the grammar of the Bangolan language. Compare the following examples that differ only in the pitch on the verb
tone_statements.locator: sec. 3 Tone, p. 6; sec. 3.1 p. 7; sec. 3.2 p. 9
tone_statements.summary: Six lexical tones (H, M, L, rising, high-falling, low-falling), many minimal pairs; tone marks verb aspect; associative floating tones noted; nothing on stress. Low-falling diacritic glyph uncertain.

sources.citation: Njeck 2003 thesis, section 1.5 Review of literature (p. 8), naming Grimes 1992 (Ethnologue), Nashipu 1989 (dialectometrical study of the Ndop plain languages), Graffin 1994 (SIL rapid appraisal survey of Bangolan) and Ndiwane 2000 (history)
sources.note: The thesis states these earlier works 'are mainly concerned with the classification of Băŋgulaŋ. There is none that has done a descriptive work on the language' (p. 8); none is a phonological description.

sources.citation: Mbah, Njeck Mathaus (2003). A phonology of Bangulan and a proposed orthography. Université de Yaoundé. x+91 pp.
sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: open copy online
sources.note: The catalog has no records and no existing statements for bang1356, and the work says nothing about stress, so there is nothing to agree with or contradict. What it does establish is that the language is tonal (six tonemic pitches), which supports classifying it as a tone language without a stress statement.

sources.citation: Mbah, Njeck Mathaus. 2003. A phonology of Băŋgulaŋ and a proposed orthography. Maîtrise dissertation, Department of African Languages and Linguistics, University of Yaoundé I (Dec. 2003), x+91 pp. (supervisors Tamanji Pius, Ndamsah Gratiana).
sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: not located online or in the libraries checked
sources.note: Nothing: no occurrence of stress/accent/prominence/intonation anywhere in the scanned text (checked with scanned-variant spellings). Chapter 4 'Tones' (pp. 46-59) describes a tone language with three level tones (H, M, L) and three contour tones (LH rising, HL falling, plus a low-falling tone), lexical minimal pairs and grammatical tone (imperative H vs progressive M on verbs); ch. 5 word structure (pp. 60-69) gives syllable/word templates with no prominence marks; ch. 6 orthography marks tone only. 'BZggularJ [Băŋgulaŋ] has no dialect' (p. 7).

sources.citation: Njeck, Mathaus [Mbah]. 2003. Phonological sketch of Bangolan. Yaoundé: NACALCO (BASAL project), November 2003, 19 pp. SIL Language & Culture Archives record 47360.
sources.note: Nothing: no stress/accent/prominence/intonation terms; 'prosodies' refers only to Firthian labialisation/palatalisation/prenasalisation. Section 5 'Tone' (pp. 16-18): 'We have identified five basic phonetic pitches on single syllables in Bangolan: three level tones, high, mid, and low; and three contour tones, low-high rising, high-low falling and low-falling' (p. 16; tone-letter diacritics garbled in the text), lexical minimal pairs (pp. 16-17), contrast chart (p. 18), one grammatical-tone contrast 'he has gone' vs 'he is going' (p. 18).

sources.note: Nothing on stress; reports 3 level + 3 contour tones, lexical and grammatical tone, all second-hand from the NACALCO sketch.

sources.citation: Freeland, Lance. 2015. A Collection of Bangolan (Mendenkye) Interlinear Texts. Yaoundé: SIL Cameroon. 28 pp.
sources.note: Seven interlinear folk/history texts in the provisional Mendenkye orthography (Njeck 2004); the Orthography note states that tone is left unmarked in the transcriptions pending further study; no description of the tone system itself (for that see the held Njeck 2003 thesis ch. 4 pp. 46-59 and sketch sec. 5 pp. 16-18: 3 level + 3 contour tones).

tone.quote: In these interlinearised texts, the original Mendenkye text is transcribed using the provisional Mendenkye orthography (Njeck 2004). [...] Tone has been left unmarked in these transcriptions. Further study is required before proposing and implementing tone in the orthography.
